newsitem.title: ERITREA: Sudanese rebels say they killed 15 Sudan soldiers.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese rebels say they killed 15 Sudan soldiers.

text.p: A Sudanese opposition alliance said on Thursday a new combined rebel force killed 15 Sudanese government soldiers in an attack in eastern Sudan on Tuesday.
National Democratic Alliance (NDA) spokesman Farouk Abu Issa told Reuters during an NDA leadership council meeting in the Eritrean capital the new force included three rebel groups.
"We have created a united military group, made up of the SPLA (Sudan People's Liberation Army), the SAF (Sudan Alliance Forces) and the Beja (Congress)," Abu Issa said.
"This armed force is now in order. In fact it carried out its first operation under the banner of the NDA on October 8 against a military garrison in Tukan, 100 km (60 miles) from Aroma," he added.
"They attacked the garrison, they put it on fire, 15 were killed. The garrison was fully controlled by our army".
He said government reinforcements were sent from Aroma and the rebels set the Tukan garrison ablaze before leaving.
He said there was one rebel casualty in the operation.
He said "joining of the gun" of separate rebel forces was the most important issue at the leadership council meeting since Monday. He said he had no information on the size of the new force.
Abu Issa said the new force had a common training camp and its leader was General Fathi Ahmed Ali, the NDA commander.

The NDA, Sudan's opposition alliance in exile, has been based in the capital Asmara since February. Eritrea broke diplomatic relations with Sudan in late 1994, accusing Khartoum of sending Moslem fundamentalist guerrillas to attack it.
